title: Hemisphere Navigation Zones — prototype for context-preserving compact sidebar and guided routing
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: As teams adopt Redwood for multiple deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private), users complain about losing workspace and routing context when switching between dashboards, rollouts, and cost views. Current left-rail is dense, offers many routes but delivers poor in-surface context continuity for multi-tenant flows (e.g., switching model rollout to a different region while viewing cost breakdowns).

Goal: Design a compact, context-preserving navigation pattern that: (1) surfaces the active context (workspace, model, route) without taking significant vertical space, (2) provides guided routing flows for common multi-step tasks (rollouts, reserve capacity, private deployment onboarding), and (3) leaves room for lightweight telemetry and quick actions (pin, favorite, start canary).

Proposal summary: "Hemisphere Navigation Zones" divides the left rail into three vertical zones: a collapsed primary zone (global anchors like Workspaces, Models, Routes), a contextual middle band that expands per selection to show task-specific micro-controls (e.g., canary traffic slider, cost filter presets), and a footer action zone holding quick workspace switch and telemetry peek. The pattern emphasizes progressive disclosure: default collapsed primary icons + badges; hover or explicit expand reveals a focused subpane with breadcrumbs and in-place microflows. Prototype explores two compact widths (56px and 92px) and a transient expansion mode that slides a 340px contextual pane over the content area rather than resizing the main canvas.

Design decisions and tradeoffs: 1) Collapsed vs persistent labels — we recommend icon-first collapsed state to preserve vertical height for long project lists, with optional persistent labels for users in accessibility mode. 2) In-place microflows vs full-page routing — microflows speed common tasks but could hide deeper settings; the prototype supports a "More settings" link that opens full route views. 3) Telemetry peek — a 3-line telemetry summary is visible in the footer zone; heavier telemetry links to the Console's observability panels so as not to overload the nav.

Accessibility: Keyboard-first traversal for all navigation zones, ARIA roles on the contextual pane, clear focus rings on expand/collapse, and a high-contrast toggle for users with low vision. We validated color contrast for badges and the telemetry sparkline placeholder.

Next steps: usability testing with 6 platform engineers, iterate interactions for overflow behavior, and align engineering on animation budget and accessibility requirements. Deliverables: Figma prototype, interaction spec, and a small front-end experiment in the Console repo that demonstrates expansion behavior and the telemetry peek API integration.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype in Figma with both 56px and 92px compact widths and expansion flows
Interaction spec documenting keyboard flows, ARIA roles, and focus order
Usability test report with at least 6 sessions and prioritized issues list
Engineering prototype PR that implements the slide-over contextual pane and telemetry footer (no backend changes required)
Accessibility checklist passed for color contrast and keyboard navigation
